newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Labor official says jobs data show strength.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Labor official says jobs data show strength.

text.p: An economist with the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday that March employment figures revealed ongoing strength in the nation's jobs market.
"I think clearly that the March data suggest a continuing strength in the labor market," BLS Economist Harvey Hamel said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
The Labor Department reported earlier that 175,000 non-farm jobs were created last month, fewer than the 293,000 added to February payrolls and slightly less than forecast.
The jobless rate dipped to 5.2 percent but Hamel characterized the rate's trend as "relatively flat" in recent months.
"I don't read too much into the tick down to 5.2 percent," Hamel said of the jobless rate. "I would just say that unemployment is remaining low."
Hamel noted an "upward trend in the course of wages" in the March data but he said "we haven't seen it as being inflationary yet."

He also pointed to strong gains in services, retail trade and manufacturing. He acknowledged weather-related job losses in the construction sector in March but said the industry has shown underlying strong growth over recent months.
